title: Exact Koszul completion and the triangulated complete locus
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$ and a finite list of global sections $b_1,\ldots,b_r$, possibly empty. Put $\mathcal J=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)\mathcal O$ and use $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $Q_m=\bigotimes_j[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{b_j^m}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $[-r,0]$, with transition $b_j$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$ in each factor, and use the natural degree-zero augmentation unit $\eta_N:N\to\Lambda(N)=R\lim_m(N\otimes^L Q_m)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], with the strict-tower derived limit of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then $\Lambda$ is an exact functor of triangulated categories and the unit commutes with shifts and maps of distinguished triangles. The locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete objects [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete] form a strictly full triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]: zero is complete; isomorphisms and all integer shifts preserve completeness; and in every distinguished triangle completeness of two vertices implies completeness of the third. No Noetherian or boundedness hypothesis is required.
